plate.note: Layout guide for a new Arche plate: the baked island model from the south, looking north and down at about 45 degrees, the whole island in frame.

scene.prompt: Photorealistic isometric diorama of the Greek island Arche, Hellenistic Greece, 3rd century BC, for 3D reconstruction. [image 1] is a 3D model of it: keep its camera, the island's outline, landforms and every building, quay, pier and road exactly where and as large as they are, and give every surface real detail. A broad limestone massif with eight wooded spurs and gullies fills the island; on its top a small ruined cyclopean ring wall round pale crags, with a narrow slot on the north and a wider timber-framed gap on the south. A narrow cliff road runs all round the coast through three alike harbour towns: stone quays and piers, a few merchant ships; on each quay a long trading house with a Doric portico; courtyard houses and storehouses with whitewashed plaster walls on low rubble bases, gabled terracotta roofs, earth streets. Olive and vine terraces low down, pine and maquis above. Bright clear sun from the upper right, crisp shadows, no haze. Sea to every edge. Zero people, no text, no pedestal.
